sentences.text: The first accused in C.C. No.286 of 1999 on the files of the Court of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class -1, Kochi filed this Revision Petition challenging the concurrent finding of conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Section 16(1)(a)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 read with Rule 50(1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules 1955.

2. Heard.
3.

The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:-
On 4.3.1999 at 5.30 p.m., PW1, the Food Inspector, purchased 750 gram of gingelly oil from the shop of the revision petitioner.
After sampling as per rules, one of the samples was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst.

The Public Analyst filed Ext. P22 report stating that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for gingelly oil under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 and therefore, the same was adulterated.
4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to 5 were examined and Exts.P1 to P26 were marked for the prosecution.
DW1 was examined and Exts.D1 and D2 were marked for the revision petitioner.
5. After evaluating the evidence, the trial court acquitted the revision petitioner for the offence of sale of adulterated food articles.
The said finding of acquittal was not challenged by the complainant.
However, the revision petitioner was convicted and sentenced by the trial court for the sale of food item without having the license under the P.F.A. Rules.
The appellate court confirmed the same.
It is borne out from the records that the revision petitioner renewed the license on 31.3.1999.
PW1 purchased the food article on 4.3.1999.

Therefore, it is proved beyond reasonable doubt that the revision petitioner sold the food article without having a valid license under the P.F.A. Rules and in the said circumstances, the conviction for the said offence does not warrant any interference by this court.
6. As regards the sentence, the learned counsel for the revision petitioner has pleaded for leniency.
The revision petitioner was aged 38 years during the relevant period. Presently, he is aged 57 years.
The revision petitioner was acquitted by the trial court for the sale of adulterated food item.
There is no previous conviction against the revision petitioner.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that the revision petitioner shall be sentenced as provided under 2nd proviso to Section 16(1) of the P.F.A.Act, to secure the ends of justice.

Accordingly, the sentence awarded by the courts below stands modified and reduced to imprisonment till the rising of the court and a fine of Rs.500/- (Rupees five hundred only) and in default to simple imprisonment for five days under Section 16(1)(a)(ii) of the P.F.A.Act read with Rule 50(1) of the P. F.A. Rules.
In the result, this revision petition stands allowed in part as above.

The revision petitioner shall surrender before the trial court on 17.03.2016 to suffer the sentence.
